title: Adaptive frugal sampler with latency-skew detection
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Goal: Reduce tracing CPU and allocation overhead in high-QPS services while preserving actionable tail traces for post-incident analysis. We will implement an "adaptive frugal sampler" that dynamically reduces sampling on stable, low-latency traffic and selectively retains higher-fidelity traces when latency skew or error signals appear. The design avoids hotpath locks and per-request heap allocations by doing lightweight probabilistic decimation in the ingress path and deferring heavy sampling decisions (span aggregation, full-span encoding) to a bounded-background worker. The feature integrates with existing tracing hooks and exposes a new metric 'tracer.decimation_rate' and a dashboard for latency-skewed sampling behavior. Expected benefits: 3-4x reduction in tracer CPU at tail events, 60-80% fewer allocations on the hotpath, and >95% preservation of top-N tail traces for high-latency incidents. Risks: transient under-sampling of very rare error modes, increased complexity of background resolution logic.
acceptance_criteria: 99th percentile tracer CPU overhead under baseline synthetic workload reduced from 2.1% -> <=0.5%
hotpath allocations attributable to tracing reduced by >=60% in alloc profile
end-to-end request latency regression <= 1ms median and <= 3ms 99th compared to control
preserve at least 95% of top-50 tail traces for windows where request latency > 1s
no schema changes required for existing trace consumers; backward compatible headers
unit tests, integration tests, and benchmark harness included with PR
steps: Run microbenchmark: current tracer overhead baseline (CPU/allocs) using workload-v2 harness
Prototype ingress decimation algorithm (one-byte token + xorshift RNG) in C++ path and measure hotpath cost
Implement bounded background resolver service that receives lightweight sample-references and performs full-span capture/encoding
Add latency-skew detector: histogram window + outlier scoring to increase sampling temporarily
Wire new metrics and create Grafana panel for decimation_rate, delayed_capture_backlog, tail_preserve_ratio
Open RFC for sampling knobs and tenant defaults; iterate with PM/SEC/Infra reviewers
Send canary rollout to low-traffic cluster and collect metrics for 72 hours
Roll out gradually and monitor SLOs and tracing-backed alerts

notes_on_tradeoffs: We accept a small increase in complexity (background resolver + batching) to eliminate per-request allocations on the hotpath.

Decimation increases the chance of missing extremely rare single-request failures; mitigation: fast-enable full-sampling for tenants that indicate incident windows via the API and retain short-term high-fidelity buffers.
We avoid changing trace schema to minimize downstream consumer work; instead we add a compact sample-reference that existing consumers can ignore.
Default aggressiveness will be conservative for enterprise customers; open to A/B tuning after canary
